mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance, reducing the cost of capital and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% in the past month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions and reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a contraction in consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a manufacturing supply shock (indicated by industrial production declining below 100.0), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to inflationary pressures and reduced corporate output.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past month signals strong labor market conditions and rising consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.0% (as measured by CPIAUCSL), it signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline from prior period
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
